label: op.api-access.add.socks5.remote
help:
Configure a remote SOCKS5 proxy

Usage: mullvad api-access add socks5 remote [OPTIONS] <NAME> <REMOTE_IP> <REMOTE_PORT>

Arguments:
  <NAME>         An easy to remember name for this custom proxy
  <REMOTE_IP>    The IP of the remote proxy server
  <REMOTE_PORT>  The port of the remote proxy server

Options:
  -d, --disabled             Disable the use of this custom access method. It has to be manually enabled at a later stage to be used when accessing the Mullvad API
  -u, --username <USERNAME>  Username for authentication against a remote SOCKS5 proxy
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Password for authentication against a remote SOCKS5 proxy
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version

label: op.api-access.add.socks5.local
help:
Configure a local SOCKS5 proxy

Usage: mullvad api-access add socks5 local [OPTIONS] <NAME> <LOCAL_PORT> <REMOTE_IP> <REMOTE_PORT>

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          An easy to remember name for this custom proxy

  <LOCAL_PORT>
          The port that the server on localhost is listening on

  <REMOTE_IP>
          The IP of the remote peer

  <REMOTE_PORT>
          The port of the remote peer

Options:
  -d, --disabled
          Disable the use of this custom access method. It has to be manually enabled at a later stage to be used when accessing the Mullvad API

      --transport-protocol <TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL>
          The Mullvad App can not know which transport protocol that the remote peer accepts, but it needs to know this in order to correctly exempt the connection traffic in the firewall.
          
          By default, the transport protocol is assumed to be `TCP`, but it can optionally be set to `UDP` as well.
          
          [default: TCP]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
